title: Streaming adapter: semantic separators + error boundary envelopes for Python SDK
creator: Laura Chen
description: Improve developer ergonomics for streaming chat completions by delivering a small, deterministic framing convention: semantic separators (lightweight tokens that mark logical response boundaries) combined with per-event error boundary envelopes. Goal is to make client-side parsing, resumability, and partial-retry semantics easier and safer for application developers without changing the underlying server-side event model.
acceptance_criteria: Python SDK exposes a StreamingAdapter class that emits typed events: MessageChunk, Separator, BoundaryError, EndOfResponse
Separator tokens are simple UTF-8 markers that can be enabled per-request via a boolean flag (enable_semantic_separators=true)
When enabled, SDK guarantees separators are inserted at sentence or paragraph boundaries (heuristic) and included in stream events to make delta-apply trivial for clients
Errors within a response are emitted as BoundaryError envelopes with stable offsets so consumers can safely retry from last confirmed Separator
Comprehensive unit tests (parser, adapter, retry stub) and integration tests against local mock stream service
Docs and one migration cookbook added to SDK docs with code examples for resumable consumers and retry recipes
No measurable >2% p90 latency increase for typical small-chat workloads in CI perf harness
design_notes: We considered two approaches: (A) richer JSON envelope for every token (more explicit but heavier), (B) tiny separator events plus minimal envelopes only for errors and checkpoints. Chosen approach B to minimize token overhead and keep streaming low-latency. Separators are opt-in to avoid changing existing contracts. Separator representation: a 3-char marker '⟮SEP⟯' (UTF-8) wrapped in a Separator event. We will provide a helper DeltaApplier on the client to simplify applying chunks across separators.
engineering_notes: Implementation plan: add StreamingAdapter to python-sdk/streaming with three layers: network event pump, semantic transform (separator insertion/recognition), consumer-facing async iterator. Adapter should support pause/resume with checkpoints keyed by (request_id, separator_seq). Add telemetry hooks for separator frequency and boundary-retry counts. Backpressure: adapter exposes awaitable drain() and exposes queue_depth metric. Prototype completed; integration tests failing on mock service timeout; investigating socket keepalive settings.
decisions: Opt for opt-in separators to preserve backward compatibility
Use a lightweight UTF marker '⟮SEP⟯' instead of numeric offsets to be resilient across encodings
Emit BoundaryError envelopes only for transient/partial-failure cases to allow safe replay semantics
tasks: Add StreamingAdapter and DeltaApplier in python-sdk
Wire new telemetry metrics (separator_count, boundary_retries) into telemetry pipeline
Create integration tests with mock-stream-service harness and golden fixtures
Write docs: streaming separators RFC + cookbook with resumable consumer example
Open RFC PR and coordinate design review with DX and Product
Perf run in CI and validate latency regression <2%
